one_liner: Salesforce B2C Commerce exposes broad REST APIs (SCAPI/OCAPI) with Account Manager and SLAS OAuth tokens, and the vendor ships an official B2C MCP server. A real instance still comes through Salesforce, though a public demo sandbox exists.
auth_notes: Account Manager API clients issue scoped JWT bearer tokens. Admin APIs use client credentials, and SLAS (OAuth 2.1) gives shopper tokens. Clients are created by an administrator in Account Manager, so self-serve user authorization is limited. The OAUTH2 primary is a judgment call.
access_notes: The API is at no extra cost for B2C Commerce customers. The only stated route to an instance is contacting Salesforce sales (third-party guide). The docs mention a shared demo sandbox and on-demand sandboxes, but the pages don't show that an individual developer can get their own credentials without an existing B2C instance and realm. This is uncertain.
blocker_notes: A B2C Commerce instance and realm are needed to create API clients. The only explicit access route in the evidence is contacting Salesforce sales. A demo sandbox is mentioned and might lower the barrier for shopper API testing, but this is unverified.

evidence.quote: Both the Admin and Shopper APIs are authorized using an access token in the form of a JSON Web Token (JWT).

The B2C Commerce API (SCAPI) is a set of RESTful APIs for building storefronts, merchant tools, and integrations on the B2C Commerce platform.
The B2C MCP server connects your AI assistant to Salesforce B2C Commerce tools, documentation, and workflow skills.
The B2C Commerce MCP Service is a fully-hosted service for linking an AI agent to real-time B2C Commerce data access.
